ingolfured/gr-tdigest.body:
Modern Python ndarray results currently pass through a Python list and one Python float per value before NumPy copies them. This change copies the existing f64 result slice directly into NumPy-owned memory. Exact values, Float64 dtype, shape, independent writable/resizable arrays and existing scalar/list/tuple behavior are preserved. The original `tdigest_rs` API and arithmetic are unchanged.

This is a standalone follow-up to #8. Review **#6 → #7 → #8 → this PR**; the base is `review/3-upstream-compatibility-gate`. The production change is limited to three output conversions in `src/py.rs`.

On NumPy 2.3.4 in single-thread WSL Linux, the six qualified nonempty CDF cases used **44.86–54.76% less time**, and the six quantile cases used **36.53–51.39% less time**. These use 64, 1,000 or 32,768 queries over fresh 8,192-input ties/separated fixtures, in both digest precisions. This measures Python conversion overhead; no accuracy improvement or Rust speedup is claimed.

All 36 fresh heldout cells remain in the evidence: 25 qualified improvements, seven neutral/noisy, two unstable and two short, with no confirmed regression. The f64 encode control was stable/neutral initially but unstable in the longer repeat (one ratio 1.1269; candidate drift 1.1285), so that repeat remains inconclusive. Empty f32 CDF, two large weights-getter cases and unresolved screen observations also remain disclosed. NumPy 1 establishes compatibility only; allocator usable bytes and peak RSS were not measured.

[Measurement method, frozen workers and per-cell results](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/tree/42d620428520a74fec8c57d5dc6d4db0f6b1920e/compat/performance/numpy-output-20261015).

Validation in Linux:

- `make lint`, `make build`, `make test`: 121 Rust tests (three existing ignored), 352 Python/coherence cases, 13 Java tests and all 91 untouched upstream tests passed.
- The optimized manylinux_2_28 ABI3 wheel passed 2,022 installed test instances across CPython 3.10–3.12, NumPy 1/2 and a Polars-free installation. Imports and native bytes were verified against the wheel. The genuine source archive and unchanged lock were checked; a separate source-rebuilt wheel is not claimed.
- Explicit installed tests passed 18 ownership/value cases on each NumPy line. All 36 frozen heldout outputs per line matched the preserved baseline exactly.
- The independent pinned upstream oracle, original lock and recorded debug/release outputs remain unchanged: 70 cases, 1,762 exact-bit and 126 NaN-class comparisons per profile. Final installed numerical fixtures ran in every support cell; expected data was not regenerated.

Validation used `d540960`; head `42d6204` differs only in README wording clarifying the inherited single-element scalar return. Production, tests and CHANGELOG are byte-identical.
ingolfured/gr-tdigest.title: Reduce NumPy output conversion overhead without changing results

ingolfured/gr-tdigest.body:
This PR completes the compatibility and delivery contract: existing applications keep `tdigest_rs.TDigest` and its original calculations; `gr_tdigest` is the opt-in modern engine. It restores the original Rust package, validates actual installed artifacts, and records measured advantages and limits.

Review the commits in this order:

- The original 91-case suite, independent 70-case exact-output fixture, 13 API checks, two optional-import checks and 32 authentic published-pickle fixtures form the **208-case compatibility gate**. Original assertions/tolerances are untouched and source checksums are enforced.
- `3b8fa69` restores lightweight `tdigest_core` with its public fields/methods. An independent export built with the original project's committed lock matches 1,762 bit comparisons plus 126 NaN classifications in each of debug/release. Git dependencies can select the package by name; old repository-root path dependencies need `src/upstream`.
- `360ad5b` restores genuine CPython 3.10 ABI3 support, declares tested Python 3.10-3.12 / NumPy 1-2 bounds, and makes Polars an optional pinned extra. `3d0182a` accepts equivalent normalized Python-version metadata. Earlier packaging fixes remove bytecode and a source-archive README collision.
- `ff73cfa` fixes a confirmed modern high-delta defect: `[0,0,100]` at delta 1,200 could collapse to a median near 33.333. A nonpositive K2Norm normalizer now retains the existing centroids. The preserved wheel fails 14 new cases with six controls passing; all 20 pass after the fix. Positive-domain calculations and the original engine are unchanged.

Latest complete-stack source `ff73cfa` passes Linux/WSL build, test and lint: **334 Python/coherence + 91 untouched original cases, 121 Rust tests, and Java**. Three pre-existing Rust tests remain ignored. The direct optimized wheel and a distinct wheel rebuilt from its unmodified normalized source archive each pass **2,022 test instances across seven isolated environments**, with no skips/xfails: six CPython 3.10-3.12 x NumPy 1/2 cells run 208 compatibility + 90 modern cases each; a Polars-free cell runs 208 + 26. Both numerical invariant audits pass on the direct wheel: 800 weighted-point digests and 1,440 compressed routes / 3,840 states. Repeated environment cases are not distinct test definitions.

Personal review CI at `25c8c16` is green.

<!-- morning-validation-20261015:start -->
The [LF checkout fix](https://github.com/ingolfured/tdigest-rs/commit/d50629973226571fae984013dda86f90f6cc1302) now passes the original raw-byte guards remotely on Windows. A subsequent [test-launcher fix](https://github.com/ingolfured/tdigest-rs/commit/57e7978d0811baed4a546ff2f08dccaeff03c321) replaces the null device with a real temporary pytest configuration and an explicit, resolved test root. It passes all 208 compatibility and 92 modern cases in Linux, plus two focused isolation controls using a symlinked temporary directory and conflicting parent configuration. Test assertions, expected counts, numerical source and build manifests remain unchanged.

The [current fork CI run](https://github.com/ingolfured/tdigest-rs/actions/runs/38693154198) passes at `57e7978`: Rust tests on all configured platforms, Python 3.10–3.12 source-interface tests on Linux/macOS/Windows, all seven wheel builds, and the installed GNU x86_64 wheel / NumPy matrix. The other platform wheels were built, not individually installation-tested.
<!-- morning-validation-20261015:end -->

Saved-state evidence uses published **0.1.0**, distinct from pinned source **0.2.0**. The original loader recompresses at default delta 300; fixtures compare restored old states. Reverse protocol-4 migration passed the tested NumPy 1 environment, while NumPy 2 protocol 5 uses a namespace absent there. The [actual upstream artifact](https://github.com/ingolfured/tdigest-rs/blob/bc1f93e15c216b14b532bb005a2a2e2e662a08f8/docs/review-refresh.md) now passes upgrade/removal/reinstall with those 32 exact restored states and 208 compatibility cases after each install. Its direct and unmodified-source-rebuilt wheels each pass 2,036 installed instances; the upstream-specific source adds two version-identity regressions. This supersedes the earlier name-only prototype for that specific artifact.

The corrected-source [matched-budget accuracy study](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/blob/8fff555623ca7a472ac38bc9066dbb81534e424d/compat/accuracy/matched-budgets-ff73cfa/RESULTS.md) measures opt-in modern K2Norm/Off at `ff73cfa` against independent original `8d9cf1`: **576 held-out dataset-policy invocations / 8,064 states**, eight distributions, three fresh seeds and both precisions. All selected storage caps and separate 2-point rank policies pass in that study, but a cap does not ensure accuracy: modern's worst queried-rank error at 1 KiB is **43.583 percentage points**. At 4 KiB, worst median rank improves while worst all-query rank can worsen. Under the separate 2-point policy, modern logical storage reaches roughly **2×** the original's. Large value errors across gaps can coexist with small rank error. Tighter policies were unavailable within the frozen grid, not proved impossible.

The [native timing follow-up](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/blob/8fff555623ca7a472ac38bc9066dbb81534e424d/compat/performance/matched-budgets-ff73cfa/RESULTS.md) uses the same frozen settings at one million values, one fresh seed and two counterbalanced blocks: all **72 processes** complete. It retains **eight distinct policy-state misses** beyond the smaller training sizes. Builds and median queries improve in measured cells, while some sequential merges are slower; normal f64 at the 2-point policy builds in 0.825/0.868× the original time but sequentially merges in 1.542/1.681×. That error policy does not match actual storage. All cells, both blocks, absolute times, k-way/CDF measurements and control drift are available; this is not a global ranking or Python-adapter speed claim. Earlier fixed-delta studies retain their historical source labels.

Release limits remain explicit: shared namespace ownership makes independent co-installation unsafe, Python 3.13+ and the wider wheel/Linux deployment matrix are unproven, Rust root-path consumers need migration, and extreme arithmetic limits remain. The new runtime checks use pinned dependencies, not an unconstrained resolver. Original imports retain the original calculation path; adapter changes can affect runtime costs, and modern-engine speedups require opt-in.

Review **#6 then #7 then #8**. These branches are stacked; rebase/retarget each dependent PR after its parent merges. #6 and #7 keep their validated code; #8 completes original Rust/runtime/artifact delivery, the later high-delta correction, and the source-labelled accuracy/performance evidence. [Upstream PR #38](https://github.com/G-Research/tdigest-rs/pull/38) now contains the actual tested package and remains draft. Its upstream CI workflow is disabled for inactivity: a maintainer must re-enable it, run the current PR and complete the required review. Fork CI cannot create the upstream-required app-backed check. No merge or release is implied.

[Review guide](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/blob/8fff555623ca7a472ac38bc9066dbb81534e424d/compat/REVIEW_GUIDE.md) | [Validation and artifact hashes](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/blob/4bb78de91f7214cb811a35b3ed4bdcb7b2fe4685/compat/validation/README.md) | [Held-out accuracy](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/blob/4bb78de91f7214cb811a35b3ed4bdcb7b2fe4685/compat/accuracy/held-out-20261015/RESULTS.md)

ingolfured/gr-tdigest.body:
The modern engine could lose observation mass, move an exact point during compression, or change answers after updates and serialization. For two equal f32 piles of weight `2**24`, adding on the left could leave its stored weight unchanged and move the median right. Weights now stay in f64 independently of mean precision. A one-input compression cluster keeps its exact mean bits and Atomic/Mixed kind.

The shared Rust corrections also cover weighted medians, scaled CDF tails, true extrema, protected-edge overlap, finite compressed means that round outside their input interval, and queries whose whole mass is subnormal. Polars applies configuration before compression and preserves it through updates and state. Weight scaling now validates every product and both mass totals before committing, so overflow/underflow returns an error with the original digest unchanged.

The costs are explicit: f32 centroids grow from **12 to 16 bytes** on the tested Linux target; f64 stays 24 bytes. Polars writes Float64 weights and reads old Float32 weights by exact promotion. TDIG v3 flag `0x08` prevents older readers silently narrowing weights that require f64; it adds no payload bytes. Explicit old-format exports retain their checked limits for mass, delta and wide edge settings.

Read the small weighted-edge, f32-mass, single-cluster, mean-bound, subnormal and transactional-scaling regressions first; then the centroid/compressor/query code and state codecs. These fixes affect the modern engine. #7 preserves the original `tdigest_rs` arithmetic separately.

The earlier audit's two order failures remain recorded; its fixed-source rerun passes. Subnormal compression loss, tiny components within normal totals, input/merge aggregate overflow and weighted-value sum overflow remain separate limits. A bounded passing matrix is not a proof for all finite inputs.

ingolfured/gr-tdigest.body:
Superseded by the replacement review series: **[#6](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/pull/6) → [#7](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/pull/7) → [#8](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/pull/8)**.

The combined implementation is now split into three coherent diffs:

1. #6: weighted-digest correctness and state preservation across frontends.
2. #7: the original Python contract in the shipped `tdigest_rs` package.
3. #8: the unchanged upstream suite, installed-wheel verification, and Linux CI.

The combined replacement stack has exactly the same production code, packaging, build wiring, and copied upstream files as this tested fix. Regression tests have been grouped by responsibility without changing assertions or parametrization; documentation has been reconciled with the new sequence.

This PR is closed only to replace its broad review scope. The branch and diff are retained. Every replacement slice passed its own WSL build and tests, and the final installed wheel passed all 91 unchanged upstream cases.

<details>
<summary>Historical implementation and validation details</summary>

The original G-Research Python suite exposed 21 failures, including a weighted digest with means `[0, 10]` and weights `[90, 10]` reporting median `5`. The shared core now returns `0`, and all **91 unchanged upstream cases pass** against both the checkout and an installed wheel.

This was the combined follow-up to diagnostic PR #3; use the replacement series above for current review and integration.

## What changed

- Fix weighted/fractional median interpolation and preserve mixed centroid provenance across merges. Compressed centroids no longer become artificial point masses during normalization.
- Ship `tdigest_rs.TDigest` in the production wheel, backed by the same Rust compressor and query code. It preserves the old defaults, dtype inference, NaN/infinity policy, and non-mutating `merge`/`update`; `gr_tdigest` retains its modern strict input and mutation contracts. Remove the test-only import shim.
- Preserve delta through copy/pickle/TDIG serialization and retain configuration and centroid kind through Polars. Correct Float32 Polars median dispatch.
- Run the upstream suite in `make test` and the Linux CI build-and-test job. Also verify all seven upstream source checksums and run all 91 cases in a fresh environment using only the installed wheel.
- Add regression coverage across Rust, Python, Polars, Java, and the CLI; update compatibility and design documentation.

## Serialization compatibility

TDIG v3 gains an optional delta header extension protected by the checksum. Readers continue to accept existing v1/v2/v3 blobs. Older readers reject the new delta flag; explicitly exporting a delta digest as v1/v2 now errors instead of losing its configuration. The infallible Rust versioned encoder documents its panic precondition.

Polars structs gain configuration and atomic-kind fields. The reader still accepts the old six-field/two-field-centroid schema using its original defaults.

## Validation

Run on Linux under WSL (Python 3.12.12, Rust 1.90.0, Java 21):

- `make build`
- `make test`: Rust, Java, Python/API coherence, and **91/91 upstream cases**
- `make legacy-wheel-test`: **91/91 upstream cases** from a clean installed wheel; package and native-extension imports verified inside that environment
- `make lint`, plus checks for the new legacy Python package and verification scripts
- `make legacy-bench-smoke`
- `git diff --check`

No upstream test, assertion, or tolerance was changed, skipped, or marked as an expected failure. One existing modern Polars test expected the incorrect median `1.6667` for `[3, 3, 1, 0]`; it now compares with NumPy's median `2`, at the same tolerance. Passing the suite establishes the tested legacy API contract, not byte-identical results for every possible input.

</details>

This PR is closed to remove the obsolete review path. Its branch and diff are retained as the diagnostic record; the historical 70-pass/21-failure result applies to this branch, not the completed replacement stack.

<details>
<summary>Historical diagnostic description</summary>

## Summary

Slice 3/4 adds a diagnostic harness for preserving the old G-Research `tdigest-rs` Python API. It runs the unchanged upstream assertions against the real compiled `gr_tdigest` extension, exposing the compatibility work that remains.

Builds on #2. This PR changes test infrastructure and documentation; it does not change the library implementation or fix the numerical/API defects recorded below.

Implementation fixes and the required Linux compatibility gate are now in follow-up #5, which targets this branch for separate review. The 70/21 results below describe this diagnostic PR's own implementation baseline.

## What's included

- `compat/tdigest-rs-upstream/`: the unchanged upstream Python tests and original benchmark, pinned to `8d9cf1fe82c5c9254e5dc9593f01717e317f4333`, with provenance and SHA256 checksums.
- `compat/tdigest-rs-strict-python/tdigest_rs/`: an import-only re-export of `gr_tdigest`. It does not emulate the old implementation or adapt numerical behavior.
- `make legacy-strict-test` / `compat-test`: rebuild the extension, run the copied assertions, and return a nonzero exit status for failures.
- `make legacy-bench-smoke` / `compat-bench`: rebuild the extension and run a **separate custom runner**, using a small smoke workload or its larger defaults. The copied upstream benchmark is retained for reference but is not executed by these targets.
- `scipy` as a development dependency for the copied tests. The unexecuted original benchmark's `joblib` dependency is not needed by these targets.
- [Compatibility status](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/blob/dd2e4d6039726f3a66fbf0b464235456a0adcf0b/compat/gr_tdigest_vs_tdigest_rs.md), linked from the README and comparison design, with the reproducible baseline and outstanding issues.

## Compatibility remains unresolved

Linux/WSL validation on 2026-10-14 collected **91 legacy cases: 70 passed, 21 failed**.

| Failure group | Cases |
| --- | ---: |
| Median accuracy / equality | 13 |
| Quantile accuracy | 1 |
| NaN / infinity handling | 5 |
| Input dtype / merge dtype handling | 2 |

These failures are not approved deviations from the legacy contract. The existing assertions and tolerances remain unchanged.

A deterministic example confirms a median defect: means `[0, 10]` with weights `[90, 10]` produce `median() == 5`, although the represented population's median is `0`. The quantile failure also exceeds an existing upstream tolerance. Neither is dismissed as harmless estimation error.

Additional probes found missing `update`, mutating `merge` behavior, and loss of `delta` after pickle/deepcopy/byte-wire round-trips. These need follow-up regression tests and fixes alongside resolution of the input/precision differences.

## Validation

Validated the correction in `dd2e4d6` on Linux under WSL with Python 3.12.12, Rust 1.90.0, Java 21, and Python dependencies from the committed `uv.lock`:

- `make build`: passed.
- `make test`: passed (Rust, Java, Python and API coherence).
- `make legacy-strict-test`: rebuilt the extension and reported **70 passed, 21 failed**, with nonzero exit status.
- `make legacy-bench-smoke`: rebuilt the extension and passed the small custom workload.
- All seven copied upstream files still match their recorded checksums.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The legacy suite remains opt-in, outside `make test` and CI while the failures are investigated. A green standard CI run does not establish legacy compatibility. Passing the old suite remains required before claiming readiness for the upstream replacement.


</details>

Expose delta construction and state/query helpers through the existing `gr_tdigest` Python interface, building on #1.

**Already merged into `master`.** This is the second foundation for the current review series: [#6](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/pull/6) → [#7](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/pull/7) → [#8](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/pull/8). Its original “2/4” title described the old review plan.

## Read this historical change in order

1. `bindings/python/gr_tdigest/__init__.py`, starting with `_resolve_size_mode` and `_resolve_scale_for_mode`: select delta versus max_size and validate the allowed options.
2. The `from_array` / `from_means_weights` wrappers: pass configuration and precision into the native API.
3. The merge wrapper, dictionary helpers, and pickle reducer: inspect the Python-facing calling and state conventions.
4. `bindings/python/tests/test_api_python.py`: focused tests for delta construction, basic pickle/deepcopy, and invalid option combinations.

## What this establishes

It adds useful Python entry points and aligns the modern default max_size at 1000. `DEFAULT_DELTA=300` matches the old compression constant.

It did not yet preserve every original API behavior: the modern merge wrapper mutates, and its accepted delta argument did not select a new merge configuration. The original API instead needs return-new-object merge/update behavior. #7 supplies that contract in the shipped `tdigest_rs` interface while preserving the modern `gr_tdigest` API.

Delta-specific state retention and numerical defects are corrected in #6; the unchanged upstream tests and installed-wheel gate arrive in #8.

ingolfured/gr-tdigest.body:
Add `delta` as an alternative compression setting in the shared Rust digest, using the normalized K2 scale (`K2Norm`) with singleton policy Off.

**Already merged into `master`.** This is the first foundation for the current review series: [#6](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/pull/6) → [#7](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/pull/7) → [#8](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/pull/8). Its original “1/4” title described the old review plan.

## Read this historical change in order

1. `src/tdigest/scale.rs`: the K2Norm scale and its normalizer.
2. `src/tdigest/compressor.rs`: delta uses the shared k-limit merge with a strict bound and bypasses the max-size cap/post-processing path.
3. `src/tdigest/tdigest.rs` and `frontends.rs`: store and propagate configuration; validate allowed combinations and merge compatibility.
4. `src/py.rs` and `quantile.rs`: expose delta/weighted construction and centroid/query helpers to Python.
5. The small CLI/JNI/wire plumbing and focused Rust regressions.

## What this establishes

A caller can select delta compression without maintaining a separate compressor. Incompatible scale/policy settings are rejected.

This foundation did not establish full legacy Python compatibility or byte-identical results. The later review found weighted-median, centroid-provenance, and serialization defects; #6 fixes those. #7 provides the original Python input/mutation contract, and #8 makes the unchanged upstream suite an acceptance gate.

G-Research/tdigest-rs.body:
Existing Python applications keep `tdigest_rs.TDigest`, its delta/dtype/state API, and the original numerical engine. The modern engine is an explicit opt-in through `gr_tdigest`. The original `tdigest_core` Rust package retains its public fields and methods; local root-path consumers must select the nested `src/upstream` package. Java retains `com.gresearch.tdigest` and its JNI contract.

The modern engine adds weighted/fractional mass, repeated and k-way merges, CDF queries and validated serialization. This refresh fixes weighted means and query boundaries, preserves f32 mass with f64 weights, makes scaling transactional, and prevents invalid high-delta K2Norm compression. These changes do not alter the original calculation path or give it modern-engine speedups.

The actual distribution is `tdigest-rs`, with provisional version **2.0.0**. It builds a cp310 ABI3 wheel, declares Python 3.10–3.12 and NumPy >=1.26.4,<3, and makes Polars 1.34.0 optional. Current upstream workflow pins, platform matrix, release graph and GNU-only allocator policy are retained.

### Validation

At source `daad31585d8d88cbffeeeba206ccfeebd733e9a1`, all local checks ran in Linux. Later commits add documentation, evidence, an LF checkout policy and test-launcher isolation; numerical source and build manifests are unchanged:

- 336 Python/coherence tests **plus all 91 untouched upstream tests**; 121 Rust tests and Java pass. Three pre-existing Rust tests remain ignored.
- The actual direct wheel and a wheel rebuilt from the unchanged normalized source distribution **each pass 2,036 installed test instances** across Python 3.10–3.12, NumPy 1/2 and a separate environment without Polars; no skips or xfails in these installed gates.
- A normal pip upgrade from the genuine published 0.1.0 wheel preserves all **32 saved states exactly against the old loader's restored states**. All 208 compatibility cases pass after upgrade and after reinstall. Uninstall removes the package-owned files.
- The installed upstream wheel passes the 800 weighted-point digest audit and 1,440 compressed routes / 3,840 states.
- Independent original-source debug/release oracle checks preserve 1,762 exact-bit comparisons and 126 NaN classifications per build over 70 cases. This is measured coverage, not a proof over every possible input.

Read the [upstream review guide](https://github.com/ingolfured/tdigest-rs/blob/bc1f93e15c216b14b532bb005a2a2e2e662a08f8/docs/review-refresh.md) and [actual upstream artifact evidence](https://github.com/ingolfured/tdigest-rs/blob/bc1f93e15c216b14b532bb005a2a2e2e662a08f8/compat/validation/upstream-daad315/README.md). The guide links the independently pinned oracle and historical personal-repository performance/accuracy evidence, with their source versions clearly identified.

<!-- morning-validation-20261015:start -->
The [LF checkout fix](https://github.com/ingolfured/tdigest-rs/commit/d50629973226571fae984013dda86f90f6cc1302) now passes the original raw-byte guards remotely on Windows. A subsequent [test-launcher fix](https://github.com/ingolfured/tdigest-rs/commit/57e7978d0811baed4a546ff2f08dccaeff03c321) replaces the null device with a real temporary pytest configuration and an explicit, resolved test root. It passes all 208 compatibility and 92 modern cases in Linux, plus two focused isolation controls using a symlinked temporary directory and conflicting parent configuration. Test assertions, expected counts, numerical source and build manifests remain unchanged.

The [current fork CI run](https://github.com/ingolfured/tdigest-rs/actions/runs/38693154198) passes at `57e7978`: Rust tests on all configured platforms, Python 3.10–3.12 source-interface tests on Linux/macOS/Windows, all seven wheel builds, and the installed GNU x86_64 wheel / NumPy matrix. The other platform wheels were built, not individually installation-tested.
<!-- morning-validation-20261015:end -->

### Measured modern-core tradeoffs

The [frozen-budget accuracy report](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/blob/8fff555623ca7a472ac38bc9066dbb81534e424d/compat/accuracy/matched-budgets-ff73cfa/RESULTS.md) and [native timing report](https://github.com/ingolfured/gr-tdigest/blob/8fff555623ca7a472ac38bc9066dbb81534e424d/compat/performance/matched-budgets-ff73cfa/RESULTS.md) measure the personal-repository modern core at `ff73cfa` against independent original `8d9cf1`; they do not measure this wheel's Python/JNI overhead. The modern configuration is K2Norm/Off and requires opt-in.

Across 8,064 held-out states, the selected storage caps and separate 2-point rank policies pass, yet modern queried-rank error reaches 43.583 percentage points at 1 KiB. Under the 2-point policy modern maximum logical storage is about twice the original's. The one-million-input timing follow-up completes 72 processes and retains eight distinct policy-state misses beyond training sizes. Build/query gains coexist with slower sequential merges. All cases, actual errors/storage, both timing blocks and unchanged-control drift remain visible; no blanket accuracy or speed claim follows.

### Remaining release decisions and limits

Keep this PR draft until upstream platform checks and rollout decisions are resolved. The upstream CI workflow is currently disabled for inactivity; a maintainer must re-enable it and run this PR. Fork CI cannot create the required app-backed check, and the required approving review is still outstanding. The recorded source-test and wheel-build matrix does not establish minimum-glibc deployment or installation of every musllinux, ARM, macOS and Windows artifact. Python 3.13+ is currently unverified and excluded by the declared range. The 2.0.0 version and publication sequence remain provisional.

The distributions `gr-tdigest` and `tdigest-rs` share import paths and must not be installed independently together. Upgrade checks stage the stated dependencies explicitly; they do not establish every unconstrained resolver outcome. Original pickle restoration still reconstructs with its historical default delta. NumPy 2 protocol-5 pickles cannot generally be rolled back into NumPy 1.

Modern speed and accuracy depend on input, merge route and storage. Historical results show real build-speed gains but also slower cases, larger centroid storage and substantial errors for separated modes. There is no universal speed/accuracy ranking or “best in the world” claim; existing applications retain the original numerical engine. Adapter changes can affect runtime costs; modern-engine speedups require opt-in.
G-Research/tdigest-rs.title: Preserve tdigest_rs compatibility and add an opt-in modern engine
